newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy gov may need confidence vote on budget - MP.
newsitem.headline: Italy gov may need confidence vote on budget - MP.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government may be forced to call a confidence vote to push a mini-budget through parliament because of the number of amendments presented, a member of parliament said on Wednesday.

Sergio Chiamparino, a member of the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) budget commission, told reporters that some 1,000 amendments, most presented by the opposition, had been admitted for debate under parliamentary rules.
"If these amendments remain, I don't see how it will be possible (to pass the mini-budget) without recourse to confidence...this is almost a given," he said.
A confidence vote would sweep away amendments.

The mini-budget, which the cabinet approved at the end of March, is for 15.5 trillion lire of budget deficit cutting measures and is aimed at helping Italy to meet tough economic criteria for joining a single European currency in 1999.
It is expected to go to the full chamber on April 28.
